_note: Content library for the campaign generator. Text fields use {slots} filled from the campaign context: {villain} {villainTitle} {faction} {region} {hub} {place} {next} {npc} {object} {objects} {monster} {motif} {material} {name}.

premises.title: The Sundered Crown
premises.logline: The old king's crown was broken into three and buried apart for good reason. {villain} has found the first piece.

objective.why: Reforged, the crown commands every soul buried under the border forts.
objective.ifLost: {villain} wears a crown of bone, and four centuries of dead soldiers stand up at once.

clock.label: The Crown Reforged
clock.onFill: The third shard is set. The barrow-line wakes.

premises.title: The Drowning Bell
premises.logline: A bell no one can find rings under the water every night, and each time it does, {region} loses another mile of coast.

objective.why: Three anchors were sunk to hold the bell silent. Two have already been cut loose.
objective.ifLost: The bell rings without stopping and the water takes the harbour towns in a single night.

clock.label: The Water Rises
clock.onFill: The last anchor parts. High tide never goes out again.

premises.title: The Long Winter
premises.logline: Winter came early to {region} and has not moved since. Something is holding it in place on purpose.

objective.why: Three embers were carried out of the first fire. Rekindled together, they break any season held by force.
objective.ifLost: The frost line reaches the lowlands and does not stop at the sea.

clock.label: The Deepening Frost
clock.onFill: The last road out of {region} closes under forty feet of snow.

premises.title: The Hollow Succession
premises.logline: The heir to {region} died three months ago. Someone is still wearing them, and the coronation is in six weeks.

objective.why: Three pieces of evidence, taken together, unmake the impostor in front of witnesses who matter.
objective.ifLost: The crown is placed on a thing that is not a person, and every noble house signs its name under it.

clock.label: Days to the Coronation
clock.onFill: The coronation proceeds. The court belongs to {villain}.

premises.title: The Green Flood
premises.logline: The forest has crossed the old boundary stones for the first time in nine hundred years, and it is not stopping at the fields.

objective.why: Three stones still stand. Re-cut and re-sworn, they hold the treaty line.
objective.ifLost: The treaty is void. Everything built inside the old wood goes back to the wood.

clock.label: The Wood Advances
clock.onFill: The last boundary stone is swallowed. {hub} has three days.

premises.title: The Ash Covenant
premises.logline: A contract signed a hundred years ago is being called in, and the collectors have started at the smallest villages in {region}.

objective.why: Three seals authenticate the contract. Break them and the whole covenant is unenforceable.
objective.ifLost: The debt is collected in full. Every soul named in the ledger is carried off on the same night.

clock.label: The Ledger Closes
clock.onFill: The account is settled. {hub} is empty by morning.

premises.title: The Wyrm's Tithe
premises.logline: {villain} has begun taking a tithe from {region}: first gold, then livestock, and this season, people.

objective.why: Three neighbouring powers each hold a token of the old alliance. Bring them together and there is an army instead of a rout.
objective.ifLost: {region} pays the tithe every season forever, and the price only goes up.

clock.label: The Next Tithe
clock.onFill: The tithe is collected. {hub} loses a generation.

premises.title: The Quiet Plague
premises.logline: People in {region} are not dying. They are forgetting, a little more each week, and something is eating what they lose.
themes: what a place is without its memory

objective.why: Three objects still hold true memory of what is being erased. They are the only evidence that will survive.
objective.ifLost: Nobody in {region} can remember there was ever anything wrong.

clock.label: The Forgetting
clock.onFill: {hub} forgets its own name, and the maps go blank.

premises.title: The Iron Road
premises.logline: An army is marching a road that was not there last spring, and it runs straight through {region} to something older than the war.

objective.why: The road is held down by three nails driven at its bends. Pull them and the road unmakes itself.
objective.ifLost: The road reaches the gate it was built for, and what is behind that gate comes out.

clock.label: The Column Advances
clock.onFill: The vanguard reaches the gate at the road's end.

premises.title: The Buried Star
premises.logline: Something fell in {region} a long time ago and was covered over carefully. The digging started again this spring.
themes: some doors were shut for us

objective.why: Three keys turn the seal. All three must turn, and only from the outside.
objective.ifLost: The seal opens from the inside instead, and {region} is the first thing it sees.

clock.label: The Dig Deepens
clock.onFill: The excavation reaches the hull, and the light goes wrong for sixty miles.

necromancer.label: necromancer
goals: to finish a resurrection that was interrupted a century ago
to prove that death is an administrative error and correct it
to raise an army that never needs feeding, then present the bill
methods: opening old battlefields and pressing what is under them into service
buying corpses through a shell company of undertakers
seeding graveyards with a slow contagion of animation
resources: a charter house of grave-robbers
three barrow-fields already emptied
a ledger of every burial in {region} for two hundred years
weaknesses: the anchoring phylactery is hidden but immobile
the binding on their servants is spoken aloud, and can be answered aloud
they cannot bear to destroy a record, even an incriminating one
lieutenants: a wight who was a magistrate and still holds court
a mortician who prepares the risen and hates them
a child-shaped thing that carries the ledger

cult_leader.label: cult leader
titles: the Voice of the Ninth Hour
goals: to complete a rite that has needed eight hundred participants and finally has them
to bring their patron partway into the world, feet first
to be the last person their god ever has to speak to
methods: converting the desperate faster than the region can replace them
buying up shrines and quietly changing what is worshipped in them
staging miracles that cost exactly one life each
resources: a congregation that includes the town watch
a shrine network across four settlements
a patron that answers, sometimes
weaknesses: the rite requires their voice, so silence them and it stalls
half the congregation is coerced, not converted
their patron is impatient and punishes delay
lieutenants: a former inquisitor who converted mid-interrogation
a smiling almoner who buys children's silence with bread
the celebrant who has read further than they were meant to

warlord.label: warlord
goals: to take and hold {region} before the spring thaw makes it defensible
to force a border that no treaty will be able to argue with
to build the state that exiled them a rival they cannot ignore
methods: taking the granaries first and the walls later
hiring every free company within a hundred miles
making examples of exactly one settlement per month
resources: four companies of drilled infantry
a siege train moving slower than the rumours about it
a quartermaster who has never lost a supply column
weaknesses: the army is loyal to pay, not to them
their supply line crosses one bridge
they will not refuse a formal challenge in front of their officers
lieutenants: a scout captain who is quietly negotiating with the other side
a siege engineer who loves the work more than the cause
a standard-bearer who believes every word

dragon_tyrant.label: dragon
goals: to formalise a protection racket into an actual sovereignty
to grow the hoard past the point where anyone could buy them out
to be owed something by every living thing in {region}
methods: taxing through intermediaries who take the blame
burning one holding a season as a demonstration
cultivating a client aristocracy that depends on them
resources: a lair no army has found
a network of kobold assessors and clerks
two noble houses already in their pocket
weaknesses: vanity, and an inability to let an insult stand
a hoard-item they will abandon a battle to protect
they honour the exact letter of a bargain even when it ruins them
lieutenants: a human factor who does the collecting and the lying
a kobold archivist with the whole ledger memorised
a knight who lost and now serves

fey_bargainer.label: fey power
goals: to collect on a promise made by people three generations dead
to move the boundary of their court a few miles further every year
to be given, freely, the one thing they cannot simply take
methods: offering exactly what each person most wants, at a price paid later
twisting old local customs into binding contract law
making the seasons a negotiating position
resources: every crossroads oath sworn in {region} for a century
a court that finds the whole affair delightful
the ability to be somewhere else instantly
weaknesses: they cannot lie outright, only mislead
iron, salt, and a guest-right honoured properly
their true name, written down by someone who was there
lieutenants: a mortal steward who has been sixteen for forty years
a hag who handles the paperwork and enjoys it
a knight of thorns bound by a promise they regret

aberrant_mind.label: aberration
goals: to finish thinking a thought that requires the whole region as scratch paper
to make a place where its rules apply instead of the ones already here
to be understood, once, by anything at all
methods: editing what people remember rather than what they do
spreading through wells, dreams, and shared meals
recruiting brilliant people by answering their favourite question
resources: a population that no longer trusts its own recollection
thralls in every trade including the temple
geometry that does not agree with the map
weaknesses: it does not understand deception performed badly on purpose
its influence thins in running water and in daylight
one thrall was left deliberately unedited, as a control
lieutenants: a physician who has been prescribing the contagion
a cartographer redrawing the region to match
a thrall who is aware and cannot say so

devil_broker.label: infernal broker
goals: to call in a century-old covenant on schedule and under budget
to establish enforceable infernal contract law in a mortal jurisdiction
to earn a promotion measured in souls per quarter
methods: buying debts nobody else wants and consolidating them
arranging accidents that are technically breaches of contract
hiring mortal lawyers who are very good and completely unaware
resources: a chain of signed instruments going back four generations
a compliant magistrate
an office nobody can find twice
weaknesses: a genuine procedural error voids the instrument
they must state the terms truthfully when asked directly
they cannot break their own contract, even to win
lieutenants: a mortal solicitor with excellent handwriting
an imp that handles filing and blackmail
a repentant co-signatory who wants out

giant_king.label: giant lord
goals: to prove a claim in the old giant order and climb back up it
to take back the high country by the measure their people used to use
to make the small folk part of the accounting again
methods: breaking the passes one at a time
demanding tribute measured in an obsolete and impossible unit
settling disputes personally and permanently
resources: a hold above the snowline
beasts that will not be turned by cavalry
a claim that other giants take seriously
weaknesses: bound by an oath-form they will not break in front of kin
the hold has one supply route
they underestimate anything smaller than a bear
lieutenants: a runecarver who does not believe in the claim
a human interpreter and hostage
a younger kin waiting for a mistake

doppelganger_ring.label: conspiracy
goals: to replace enough of {region}'s officials that replacement stops being necessary
to inherit a legitimate government rather than overthrow one
to make one specific person's signature theirs
methods: substitution, slowly, starting with people nobody visits
keeping the originals alive somewhere as reference
letting the real institutions do the actual work
resources: seats on the council
the originals, in a cellar, catalogued
an alibi for everyone
weaknesses: the copies share information poorly and imperfectly
a detail of the original's habits they never get right
the originals are kept alive, and can be found
lieutenants: a copy who prefers the borrowed life to their own
the handler who assigns the faces
an original who was turned rather than replaced

factions.name: the {settlement} Watch
factions.goal: keep order without admitting how bad it has got
factions.offers: official cover and a key to the gate
factions.demands: no bodies in the street and no questions in public

factions.name: the Carters' Compact
factions.goal: keep the roads profitable and open
factions.offers: fast travel, cargo space, and every rumour on the route
factions.demands: protection on one specific run nobody will take

factions.name: the Grey Almonry
factions.goal: feed and shelter more people than it can afford to
factions.offers: healing, safe beds, and the truth as they know it
factions.demands: that the party never leave a settlement worse than they found it

factions.name: the Kettle Society
factions.goal: recover and catalogue what the old world left buried
factions.offers: maps, translations, and identification of anything you dig up

factions.name: the House of Reeds
factions.goal: restore a family name ruined two generations ago
factions.offers: money, introductions, and a house to sleep in
factions.demands: public credit for anything the party achieves

factions.name: the Quiet Hand
factions.goal: run every illegal trade in the region without violence, if possible
factions.offers: contraband, forged papers, and people who owe them
factions.demands: a favour to be named later, and it will be named

factions.name: the Ninth Vigil
factions.goal: finish a war that officially ended forty years ago
factions.offers: steel, veterans, and a fortified position
factions.demands: that the party take a side in public

factions.name: the Cold Assembly
factions.goal: govern by consensus and outlast whatever is happening

factions.name: the Verge Wardens
factions.goal: hold the boundary between the settled land and what is beyond it
factions.offers: guides, safe camps, and knowledge of the deep country
factions.demands: that nothing be brought back across the line

factions.name: the Gilded Ledger
factions.goal: own the region's debt and therefore the region
factions.offers: unlimited funding at a reasonable rate

borderland.label: the borderland
features: a line of half-manned watchtowers
a river that used to be a border and is now just a river
burned fields nobody has replanted
an old military road going the wrong way

coast.label: the coast
features: a drowned village visible at low tide
salt marsh that swallows anything heavier than a person
a lighthouse keeping a schedule nobody set
shipwrecks arranged in a line that looks deliberate

highland.label: the high country
features: a pass that closes without warning
terraced fields abandoned mid-harvest
cairns marking something other than graves
a glacier with a road under it

heartland.label: the settled country
features: prosperous villages a day's walk apart
a canal with too much traffic
hedgerows older than the kingdom
a shrine at every crossroads and no priests

forest.label: the great wood
features: boundary stones the wood has grown around
charcoal camps gone quiet
a clearing that is never in the same place
trees marked with a script nobody local can read

wasteland.label: the waste
features: glassed ground in a perfect circle
wind that carries voices in the wrong language
salt flats with foundations under them
a canyon that was cut in one afternoon

funnel_to_hub.label: Funnel to hub
funnel_to_hub.note: A tight scripted opening, a settlement to breathe in, independent spokes, then the climax.

gated_sandbox.label: Gated sandbox
gated_sandbox.note: One region, no exit. The locations are fixed, the objectives float across them.

hub_and_spoke.label: Hub and spoke
hub_and_spoke.note: A settlement at the centre and independent missions radiating out. Forgiving of absent players.

branch_reconverge.label: Branch and reconverge
branch_reconverge.note: Three routes to the same climax. Real agency without three times the prep.

hexcrawl_mega.label: Hexcrawl plus megadungeon
hexcrawl_mega.note: Procedural travel and attrition feeding one very large site.

act_structure.label: Act structure
act_structure.note: Chronological acts rather than places. Urban, factional, intrigue-driven.

node_investigation.label: Node investigation
node_investigation.note: A clue graph. The order emerges from play; every conclusion has three ways in.

linear.label: Linear
linear.note: Chapter one to the end, no branching. Short, tightly plotted, easy to run.

one_shot.label: One shot
one_shot.note: A single sitting: a hook that lands in the first ten minutes, one location worth exploring, and a confrontation that settles it before the night is out.

dungeonKinds.label: Vault / Tomb
origins: raised over the barrow of a king whose name was struck out
cut as a prison and re-consecrated as a grave
built by a guild that buried its own secrets with its masters

dungeonKinds.label: Lair
origins: a natural cave enlarged by something with claws
an old cellar the country grew over
a hollow under a fallen god-statue

dungeonKinds.label: Ruin
motifs: ivy that grows the wrong direction
origins: a monastery abandoned in a single night
a manor that burned with the family inside
an outpost that lost its war quietly

dungeonKinds.label: Stronghold
origins: a border keep that changed hands three times
a customs house fortified past all reason
a garrison built to watch something that is still there

dungeonKinds.label: Desecrated temple
motifs: prayer strips in a dead script
origins: a shrine rededicated by force
a cathedral built over an older, worse altar
a hermitage that answered the wrong prayer

dungeonKinds.label: Delve / mine
origins: a shaft sunk chasing a seam that turned into something else
a company mine abandoned after the third collapse
a delve that broke into a room nobody dug

dungeonKinds.label: Wreck
origins: a trader driven onto the rocks with its cargo intact
a warship that sank at anchor with no survivors
a hull that washed up already empty

dungeonKinds.label: Planar pocket
motifs: a smell of copper and cut grass
origins: a bubble of somewhere else pressed into a hillside
a house that only has an inside
a stair that goes down further than the hill is tall

dungeonKinds.label: Megadungeon
motifs: cold air moving from somewhere below
materials: layered construction from three different centuries
origins: a city that was buried on purpose
a vault complex that outgrew its purpose
a shaft that was a temple, then a prison, then a mine

threshold: The way in: {material} steps down under a lintel carved with a warning in a script three centuries out of use. {motif} has drifted into the corners.
A doorway of {material}, propped open with a wedge somebody drove in recently. The air coming out is colder than the air going in.
The entrance hall stands open to the sky where the roof fell. {motif} lies over everything in an even layer, and there are fresh tracks through it.
junction: Four passages meet under a sagging arch of {material}. Someone has scratched tally marks at eye height on every one.
A landing where the stair turns. Drips from above have cut a channel through {motif} on the floor.
A wide corridor of {material} with alcoves down both sides, all of them empty, all of them the right size for a person.
encounter: A long room of {material}. Furniture has been dragged into a rough barricade at the far end and abandoned there.
A vaulted chamber where {motif} has been swept into piles, as if something tidy lives here.
The floor here is a foot deep in cold water. Whatever is in the room is standing in it, comfortably.
A hall with a gallery running around it at half height. Good ground for the things already up there.
puzzle: Six {material} pillars, each carved with a different phase of the same event, and a socket in the floor that expects them in an order.
A door with no handle and a poem cut into it. The last line is missing and there is a chisel on the floor.
A dry fountain with nine spouts, and a valve wheel for each, and one basin that must fill before the far door unlocks.
trap: A corridor of {material} flagstones, three of which sit a finger's width proud of the rest.
A gallery hung with old chain. Some of it is holding up the ceiling.
A narrow stair with a scored groove down the centre, worn by something heavy travelling it repeatedly at speed.
treasure: A strongroom, its door already forced. Whoever opened it took the obvious things and missed the rest.
A collapsed store-chamber where {motif} half-buries crates stamped with a merchant house that no longer exists.
A shrine-niche where offerings were left and never collected, decades of them.
lore: Wall paintings in flaking pigment run the length of the room, telling a story that stops abruptly two thirds along.
A records room. Damp has taken most of it, but not all, and the surviving pages are the interesting ones.
Someone died here writing on the wall in charcoal, and got fifteen words down.
empty: An empty chamber of {material}. Cold, quiet, and the only sound is water somewhere below.
A store-room stripped to the shelves. {motif} on the floor is undisturbed.
Living quarters, long abandoned. Bedding rotted to fibre, a cup, a boot, nothing worth carrying.
A hall too big for its purpose, echoing, with nothing in it at all.
haven: A barred side-chamber with a spring, a cold hearth, and signs of recent, careful occupation.
A cell that locks from the inside, which is the point.
A high gallery, defensible, with a view of the approach and someone already in it.
shortcut: A collapsed wall opens onto a passage that runs back toward the entrance, once you clear it from this side.
A winch-lift, still rigged, that can be brought up but only from here.
A barred door with the bar on this side, opening straight onto the approach road.
boss: The chamber the whole place was built around: {material} rising to a vault, {motif} in drifts against the walls, and a floor kept deliberately clear.
A flooded rotunda with a raised dais at its centre, and everything in the room angled to face it.
A hall of {material} pillars, half of them broken, arranged so that anyone entering is seen long before they see.

dressings: A cold draught moves through steadily; something further in is open to the air.
The walls are damp to the touch and the damp is warm.
Every surface at knee height has been rubbed smooth by decades of passing traffic.
There are tallies scratched by the door, and the count reaches four hundred and stops.
Somewhere below, at irregular intervals, something heavy is set down.
The dust here has been disturbed within the last day.
A smell of old smoke that has nothing to burn.
The light behaves oddly at the edges of the room, arriving a half-second late.
Rats have made a road through here and will not use one particular corner.
Old bloodstains, scrubbed at, not successfully.

traps.name: Scything blade
traps.telegraph: a clean horizontal groove in both walls at hip height
traps.effect: 2d10 slashing, DC 14 Dexterity save for half
traps.consequence: the mechanism resets audibly, and everything nearby now knows where you are

traps.name: Collapsing floor
traps.disarm: DC 15 Thieves' Tools or simply spanning it
traps.effect: a 20 ft drop, 2d6 bludgeoning, DC 13 Dexterity save to catch the lip
traps.consequence: whoever falls is separated from the party and lands somewhere with its own occupants

traps.name: Poison needle lock
traps.telegraph: a keyhole with a bright, un-tarnished rim
traps.effect: 1 piercing plus 3d6 poison, DC 15 Constitution save for half
traps.consequence: the poisoned character has disadvantage on the next long stretch until treated

traps.name: Sealing door and rising water
traps.telegraph: a drain grate and a waterline stained a foot up the wall
traps.disarm: DC 16 Strength to hold the door, or find the sluice
traps.effect: the room floods over six rounds
traps.consequence: gear is soaked, torches are out, and the next room is entered wet and cold

traps.name: Glyph of alarm and binding
traps.telegraph: a faint scorch outline on the threshold
traps.effect: DC 14 Wisdom save or restrained for 1 minute
traps.consequence: the alarm carries, and reinforcements arrive in 1d4 rounds

traps.name: Falling portcullis and murder holes
traps.telegraph: a slot in the ceiling and holes above the corridor
traps.disarm: DC 14 Thieves' Tools on the counterweight
traps.effect: the party is split, and 1d4 attackers fire from above
traps.consequence: the split lasts until the winch is found, two rooms away

traps.name: Crushing walls
traps.telegraph: vertical scrape marks the full height of the corridor
traps.disarm: DC 16 Thieves' Tools, or jam it with something solid
traps.effect: 4d10 bludgeoning over three rounds unless stopped
traps.consequence: whatever is used to jam it is destroyed

traps.name: Spore bloom
traps.telegraph: a pale fringe of growth around a doorway
traps.effect: DC 13 Constitution save or poisoned for 1 hour
traps.consequence: the poisoned condition makes the next social encounter noticeably harder

puzzles.name: The order of the seasons
puzzles.premise: Four reliefs must be turned to show the seasons in the order this place used, which is not the order anyone uses now.
puzzles.solution: the mural in the lore room shows the old calendar starting at first frost
puzzles.alternate: DC 16 History, or DC 18 Thieves' Tools to force the mechanism
puzzles.failure: the mechanism jams for an hour and something is alerted

puzzles.name: The weighed name
puzzles.premise: A scale, a set of lead letters, and a door that opens when the correct name is weighed out.
puzzles.solution: the name is written on the founder's coffin plate elsewhere in the site
puzzles.alternate: DC 15 Investigation on the discarded letters to work out what is missing
puzzles.failure: the wrong weight drops the counterweight and seals the room for ten minutes

puzzles.name: Nine spouts, one basin
puzzles.premise: Nine valves, one basin, and only one combination fills it before it drains.
puzzles.solution: the drain rate is written on the pipework in a maintenance hand
puzzles.alternate: DC 16 Arcana to freeze the drain, or plug it with anything
puzzles.failure: the overflow floods the corridor behind them

puzzles.name: The unlit lamp
puzzles.premise: Eleven lamps, ten already burning, and a door that will not open while any of them is lit by ordinary fire.
puzzles.solution: the eleventh must be lit with light rather than flame, and then all of them snuffed at once
puzzles.alternate: DC 15 Arcana, or a well-argued use of any light cantrip
puzzles.failure: the lamps relight themselves and the room grows warmer each attempt

puzzles.name: The false inventory
puzzles.premise: A ledger lists twelve items stored here. Eleven are present. The door wants the twelfth.
puzzles.solution: the twelfth was taken by a previous intruder whose body lies two rooms on
puzzles.alternate: DC 17 Investigation to identify the substitution and forge it
puzzles.failure: the room's guardian is roused, having been listed as item twelve

puzzles.name: The echoed word
puzzles.premise: A word must be spoken here that was last spoken here, and the room remembers.
puzzles.solution: the word is recoverable from the charcoal writing left by the dying scribe
puzzles.alternate: DC 16 Perception to hear the room still whispering it
puzzles.failure: the room answers with its own word, and everyone who hears it takes 2d6 psychic damage

hazards: The floor of this section is rotten through; treat it as difficult terrain and roll for a drop each time a fight moves across it.
Bad air. After ten minutes, a DC 12 Constitution save each hour or gain a level of exhaustion.
The cold is severe enough to matter. No natural healing on a rest taken here.
Standing water conducts what is in it; lightning and cold effects have their radius doubled here.
Loose ceiling. Any thunderous noise brings down 2d6 bludgeoning on a random point in the room.
The growth on the walls reacts to light and closes passages behind a lit torch.
loreObjects: a burial plate naming a family the party has already met in {hub}
a work roster showing {faction} paid for labour here last season
a letter, unsent, from {npc} refusing an offer from {villain}
a map with {next} circled and a note reading 'not until the third'
a devotional carving of the thing {villain} actually serves, rendered honestly
a child's drawing of the same symbol found on the bodies in {hub}
a survey chain and notebook recording a measurement that cannot be right
an inventory listing {object} as removed for safekeeping, with a destination
clueTemplates: A body here still holds a writ of passage stamped for {next}, dated for a week from now.
Scratched into the wall in a hurry: a route to {next} and the words 'do not use the front'.
{npc} is here, alive, and will trade what they know about {next} for a way out.
A courier's satchel, its seals broken, containing orders that name {next} and the hour they are expected.
A tally of shipments, all of them going to {next}, all of them signed with {villain}'s mark.
The prisoners here were taken from near {next} and can describe its approaches in detail.
A tool left behind that was made in {next} and nowhere else, still warm from use.
Someone has been keeping a diary. The last entries are about being reassigned to {next}.
entryHooks: {npc} asks for help outright, in public, having run out of quieter options.
The party is followed here, and the followers do not survive to explain why.
A survivor arrives in {hub} with the news and one useful detail.
The party is paid to do something ordinary here, and the ordinary thing goes wrong immediately.
{faction} needs a witness they can trust, and the party is the only party available.
Something the party did in the previous chapter has consequences that are waiting here.
The road is closed and this is the only way through.
{villain}'s people get here first and the party arrives during the raid.
exitStakes: If the party leaves without finishing, {villain} gets a full season's use out of this place.
Whatever is left alive here follows them to the next chapter and arrives first.
{faction}'s attitude toward the party shifts hard, in whichever direction the party earned.
The clock advances by two segments and the region notices.
The survivors carry a warning, and the next site is ready for them.
Somebody in {hub} pays for the party's decision here, by name.

problems: the well has gone brackish and the priest will not say why
a third of the working-age population left in one week and did not say where
the militia captain has started arresting people for things that have not happened yet
two families are one insult away from a feud that will burn the place down
the granary is empty and the ledger says it is full

rivalKinds.label: a rival free company
rivalKinds.wants: the same {objects} the party is chasing, to sell to the highest bidder
rivalKinds.method: moving fast, paying for information, and arriving first
rivalKinds.crosses: {villain} wants the {objects} used; the company wants them sold, and a sold {object} is one {villain} has to buy back
rivalKinds.offers: muscle, a second front, and everything they have already scouted
rivalKinds.demands: a cut, and first claim on the next {object} found
rivalKinds.ifAllied: Two crews can cover twice the ground: one optional chapter can be handled offscreen by the company, at the cost of whatever they keep from it.
rivalKinds.ifCrossed: They sell the party's route and timing to {villain}, who is waiting at the next site.
rivalKinds.leverage: They work for money, and {villain} has more of it. Outbid them once and they stay bought.

rivalKinds.label: a crown investigator
rivalKinds.wants: {villain} taken alive and tried, with the {objects} entered as evidence
rivalKinds.method: warrants, subpoenas, and the patient accumulation of testimony
rivalKinds.crosses: {villain} can survive a trial. A trial takes months, and the clock does not stop for procedure
rivalKinds.offers: legal cover, access to sealed records, and the authority to open doors
rivalKinds.demands: that nothing be destroyed and nobody be killed who could testify
rivalKinds.ifAllied: Charges stick. The ending shifts toward a public, permanent resolution rather than a body in a hole.
rivalKinds.ifCrossed: The party are the ones with warrants out, and every settlement becomes harder to work in.
rivalKinds.leverage: They must follow their own rules. Hand them a procedural excuse and they will act on it.

rivalKinds.label: a militant order
rivalKinds.wants: the same thing the party wants, and is willing to burn {region} down to get it
rivalKinds.method: purges, cordons, and the removal of anything that might be tainted
rivalKinds.crosses: {villain}'s plan dies with the region, and the order is entirely willing to trade one for the other
rivalKinds.offers: zealots who do not break, and the only people who will walk into the worst places
rivalKinds.demands: that the party stand aside from what comes after the victory
rivalKinds.ifAllied: The villain falls faster and harder, and the epilogue is uglier: the order keeps what it takes.
rivalKinds.ifCrossed: They add the party to the list of things to be cleansed, and they are thorough.
rivalKinds.leverage: Their doctrine is written down. Show them a reading of it that binds their hands.

rivalKinds.label: the antagonist's former partner
rivalKinds.wants: {villain} to suffer, personally, and does not much care what it costs {region}
rivalKinds.method: knowing exactly where {villain} is weak and spending other people to prove it
rivalKinds.crosses: they know the plan from the inside, which makes them the most useful and most dangerous person in the story
rivalKinds.offers: the truth about {villain}: the weakness, the schedule, the names
rivalKinds.demands: to be there at the end, and to be the one who does it
rivalKinds.ifAllied: The party skips a whole layer of investigation, and inherits a partner who will not stop when they should.
rivalKinds.ifCrossed: They go it alone, force the confrontation early, and lose, handing {villain} a warning.
rivalKinds.leverage: They want witnesses more than they want to win. Offer an audience.

rivalKinds.label: a profiteering house
rivalKinds.wants: the crisis to continue exactly long enough to corner the market it created
rivalKinds.method: buying scarcity, financing both sides, and owning the roads
rivalKinds.crosses: {villain} winning ends the crisis, and an ended crisis is an ended profit
rivalKinds.offers: money, supply, transport, and doors into rooms the party cannot afford
rivalKinds.demands: that certain routes stay closed and certain rivals stay ruined
rivalKinds.ifAllied: The party is never short of resources, and every settlement they save ends up owing the house.
rivalKinds.ifCrossed: Prices double, doors close, and a bounty appears that nobody will admit to funding.
rivalKinds.leverage: Show them a ledger where the villain's victory costs more than the party's does.

rivalKinds.label: a rival claimant

rivalKinds.crosses: there is one prize and two claims on it; both cannot be satisfied
rivalKinds.offers: troops, a banner to fight under, and a legitimate face for whatever the party does
rivalKinds.demands: that the party's victory install them at the end of it
rivalKinds.ifAllied: The finale has an army in it, and the region wakes up under a new power the party chose.
rivalKinds.ifCrossed: They cut a deal with {villain} instead, and the last chapter has two enemies in it.
rivalKinds.leverage: Their claim depends on being seen as the better option. Make that publicly untrue.

rivalKinds.label: an obsessive collector
rivalKinds.wants: the {objects} preserved and locked away, unused, forever
rivalKinds.method: buying, stealing, and occasionally entombing the people who used them
rivalKinds.crosses: {villain} intends to use the {objects}, which to the collector is a kind of murder
rivalKinds.offers: identification, history, and the one fact about the {objects} nobody else knows
rivalKinds.demands: every {object}, afterwards, with no exceptions and no copies
rivalKinds.ifAllied: The party learns what the {objects} really are, and hands away the only thing that could stop a sequel.
rivalKinds.ifCrossed: The collector reaches the next {object} first and it is simply gone, vault-sealed, unreachable.
rivalKinds.leverage: Offer them something rarer. There is always something rarer.

rivalKinds.label: an opportunist warlord

rivalKinds.method: taking undefended ground and daring anyone to come and get it
rivalKinds.crosses: {villain} needs {region} intact to use it; the warlord is busy eating it
rivalKinds.offers: an army, a border nobody can cross, and a very simple kind of help
rivalKinds.demands: the land they have taken, permanently, and no questions about how
rivalKinds.ifAllied: The map is safer and smaller: the party gains a wall at their back and loses the people behind it.
rivalKinds.ifCrossed: A second war opens across the party's supply line at the worst possible moment.
rivalKinds.leverage: They fear being caught between two forces. Show them the other jaw closing.

They arrive midway through, from another direction, and the party has a few rounds to decide whether that is good news.

They left a message scratched where the party would find it: a warning, an offer, or a boast, depending on how the last meeting went.
They have cleared the first third of the site and stopped, because what they found convinced them to wait for someone else to go first.
One of theirs is here alone, hurt, and separated from the rest. What the party does about it is remembered.
They got what they came for an hour ago and are on their way out. The party can let them pass, follow, or stop them.
They are negotiating with the occupants when the party walks in, and both sides turn around.

Badly. Somebody drew, nobody died, and now there is a debt on one side of it.
As rescuers. {rival}'s people pull the party out of something, and make sure the party knows the price is not settled.
Through their reputation first: three chapters of the party finding {rival} was there yesterday, before ever seeing their face.

openings: Session one opens on the road into {hub}, late in the day, with the weather turning. The party shares the last miles with a carter who talks too much, and half of what he says about {region} turns out to matter. The gate is manned by too few people asking too many questions, and somewhere behind the party, out of sight, {villain}'s people are on the same road.

Start in the common room of the inn at {hub}, the night the news arrives. Let the players order drinks and introduce themselves before the door opens; whoever carries the news is bleeding, and what they say in front of the whole room is the campaign's first clue. Everyone hears it. Not everyone wants it heard.

Open mid-journey: the party has been travelling through {region} for three days on other business when they find the first sign that something is wrong, blocking the road where it cannot be ignored. {hub} is the nearest place with walls, beds, and answers, and by the time they reach it, word of what they found has somehow arrived first.

Begin with the job that was supposed to be simple: an escort, a delivery, a survey, paid for by {npc} and worth exactly enough to take. It goes wrong at the edge of {region} in a way that is clearly not an accident, and the survivors' road leads to {hub}.

Open on the aftermath: the party arrives at a place where {villain}'s people finished their work an hour ago. What is left tells them three things: what was taken, which way they went, and that whoever did it was not worried about being followed. {hub} is where the trail points.

One PC is from {region} and left for a reason; the campaign is the reason, older and larger than they knew.

ambush: The road out here is older than the kingdom, and it shows: worn cobbles, leaning mile-stones, hedges grown high enough to hide anything. You have been walking it long enough to stop watching the hedges. That is, of course, when the first arrow comes.

It is a good day for travel, which you will remember later with some bitterness. The road narrows where a stream cuts under it, the trees lean close, and the birdsong stops all at once, the way it does when something else got there first.

Carts pass you heading the other way, more of them than seems right, and none of the drivers will meet your eyes. A mile on, you find the reason: the road ahead is blocked, and the people blocking it have been waiting for someone. Possibly you.
arrival: {region} announces itself slowly: the fields get thinner, the shrines get more frequent, and the people you pass stop asking where you are headed and start telling you to turn around. By the time you understand what they meant, the road behind you is no longer an option.

You cross into {region} in the late afternoon, and the country changes under you like a held breath. Whatever is wrong here has been wrong for a while; you can read it in the unharvested fields and the doors that close as you pass.

The last waypost before {region} has been painted over with a single word of warning. Past it, the land is beautiful and quiet and entirely too empty, and the way you came in does not look like it plans to let you back out.
hub: {hub} appears around the last bend: walls that have been repaired more often than built, smoke from a hundred chimneys, and a gate that is open but watched. Whatever else is happening in {region}, this is where people still gather, trade, argue, and hope. It will do for a base. It may have to.

You reach {hub} as the light goes, and the town takes you in the way towns like this do: warily, then all at once. There are beds here, and work, and people who know more than they say. The talk in the taproom stops when you enter, and starts again a note lower.

{hub} is busier than a town this size should be, and more frightened. Refugee carts in the market square, notices three deep on the board, and a watch that checks faces at the gate. Somebody here knows what is going on. Probably several somebodies, and they will not all tell the same story.
site: {place} is exactly where the directions said it would be, which is somehow worse. It sits in the land like a splinter, older than everything around it, and the path to it is more worn than an abandoned place has any right to be.

You smell {place} before you see it: cold air, old stone, something underneath both. The locals gave it a wide berth for generations and the land shows it, the fields ending in a clean line a half mile out, as if by agreement.

Whatever {place} was built for, it was built to last, and it has: through weather, war, and abandonment, down to this moment, with you standing at the edge of it deciding which way in. There are tracks here newer than any story about the place.
event: Some days announce themselves as trouble from the first bell. This is not one of them. It is ordinary right up until it is not, and when it turns, it turns fast, in front of witnesses, with everything you care about in the room.

You had plans for today. So did everyone else involved, which is precisely the problem: too many intentions in one place, all of them on a schedule, and yours is the only party that has not rehearsed.

It begins with a crowd, the way these things do: everyone looking at the same thing, nobody yet understanding it. You have perhaps a minute of that confusion to spend before the situation notices you back.
region: The maps of {region} agree on the towns and argue about everything in between. You are heading into the in-between: days of open country, weather with opinions, and the knowledge that out here, help is whatever you brought with you.
The road gives out a day past the last farm, and after that {region} is track, ford, and guesswork. It is beautiful country, if you can keep your eyes off the tree line long enough to notice.

Setting out across {region} feels less like travel and more like trespass. The country watches. Old cairns mark turnings nobody takes anymore, and the silence has a settled, proprietary quality, as if you are the first noise in years.
investigation: The facts do not fit, and everyone you ask arranges them differently. Somebody in this tangle is lying, somebody is mistaken, and at least one person is telling the truth to the wrong people. The only way through is to pull a thread and follow it.

It would be easier if there were a monster. Monsters are simple. What you have instead is a town full of accounts that almost agree, a timeline with a hole in it, and the growing certainty that the hole is person-shaped.

Start with what you know for certain, which is not much: something happened, someone arranged it, and the arranging took money, access, and nerve. Money leaves ledgers. Access leaves keys. Nerve leaves witnesses.
climax: Every road you have taken, every clue carried out of the dark, every name traded and favour spent, has pointed here: {place}. It stands ahead of you exactly as terrible as the stories said, and somewhere inside it, this ends, one way or the other.

There is no ceremony to arriving at {place}. The land simply runs out of other things to be, and there it is: the last place, the one under all the others. You have what you have, you know what you know, and the door is not locked. It was left open for you.

{place} has known you were coming for longer than you have. That is the plain truth of it, and you can feel it in the stillness as you approach: not the quiet of emptiness, but the quiet of something that has finished its preparations.

ambush: Survive the road, and find out who wanted you stopped badly enough to pay for it.
Get through in one piece, then follow whoever attacked you back to wherever they sleep.
Protect what you are travelling with, and take at least one attacker able to answer questions.
arrival: Find out what has gone wrong in {region}, and find shelter before dark does.
Reach safety, learn the shape of the trouble here, and discover why the way back is closed.
Get your bearings, find who is still willing to talk, and work out what this country is so afraid of.
hub: Make {hub} yours: find lodging, find work, and find out who actually knows what is happening.
Learn who runs {hub}, who fears whom, and which of the rumours in the taproom is worth chasing.
Set up a base in {hub}, earn enough trust to be told the truth, and pick your first road out.
site: Get into {place}, learn what {villainTitle} wants with it, and get out with proof.
Find out why {place} matters to the enemy, and take away whatever it is they are protecting there.
Clear {place}, or at least come back knowing what is inside and what it will cost to finish.
event: Keep the worst from happening in front of you, and be seen to be on the right side of it.
See it through with the fewest people hurt, and come away knowing who arranged it.
Hold your nerve, protect who you can, and turn the day to your advantage.
region: Cross {region} with your supplies, your health, and everyone you started with.
Get across the open country alive, and learn the land well enough to cross it again in a hurry.
Make the far side of {region} before the weather or the wildlife makes the decision for you.
investigation: Follow the clues to a name you can prove, in front of people with the power to act on it.
Find out who is behind it, how it was done, and where the trail goes next.
Sort truth from rumour, name the guilty, and do not let the trail go cold while you argue.
climax: End it: face {villainTitle} in {place}, and finish what the whole road has been leading to.
Get to the heart of {place}, stop {villainTitle} before the last piece falls into place, and get out alive.
Bring everything you have learned to bear, break {villainTitle}'s design, and decide what {region} becomes after.

goalObjectiveHints: Word in {hub} says one of the {objects} is hidden somewhere here.
If the stories are true, a {object} waits inside, and the enemy knows it too.
The rumours agree on one thing: a {object} is here, for whoever reaches it first.
npcConnections: Owes {npc} money and will not discuss it.
Is the only person in {hub} that {npc} actually trusts.
Has been quietly writing to {villain}'s people for a year.
Lost family at {place} and cannot go back there.
Will vouch for the party to {faction} once, and only once.
Knows {npc} is lying and has said nothing yet.
